findings.problem: ECHOLET_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS was removed from every operator-facing compose/env/script file, but the Go field that binds it (env:"ECHOLET_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS" envDefault:"60") still exists and is still read if an operator sets the variable anyway.
findings.impact: An operator who copies an old env file, or sets the variable from muscle memory, will have it silently accepted and read exactly as before - it changes only the frequency of two debug log lines, never anything observable. Not a regression (identical to pre-task behaviour for anyone who still sets it), but the removal is not airtight without a matching source change.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the CleanupIntervalSec field from config.go and the corresponding NewCleanupService parameter, so an operator-set variable is either ignored outright or rejected at startup - whichever a future task with tests decides. Out of scope for a documentation-only task per the dispatch's explicit instruction to report and stop rather than touch Go source.
